title: Impact Assessment Template
summary: Tell the story of your research impact with clarity and confidence. These guidelines walk you through capturing evidence, describing engagement activities, and presenting a compelling case study.

details.who: Researchers documenting impact for funders, internal reviews, or institutional storytelling.
details.what: A structured set of guidelines for crafting clear, evidence-informed case studies that highlight pathways to impact. Walk through how to capture evidence, describe engagement, and present credible impact stories.
details.outcomes: A well-structured case study demonstrating real-world research outcomes and engagement.

author: Research Impact Canada

title: Impact Indicators: Overview & Menu
summary: How do you know if your research is making a difference? This tool helps you identify and develop research output and outcome indicators linked to societal impact.

details.who: Academics and research units wanting to track and communicate societal impact.
details.what: A practical guide explaining what impact indicators are and how to write them, plus an inspirational menu of example outputs and outcomes that can be tailored to different research contexts.
details.outcomes: A set of tailored impact indicators for tracking progress toward your research goals and societal ambitions.

author: Erasmus University Rotterdam

title: Flows of Knowledge: Impact Assessment Method
summary: A clear and simple framework for designing your own research impact assessment plan, focused on non-academic impacts on policy, practice, and wider society.

details.who: Researchers and research teams carrying out impact assessment at the end of a project.
details.what: An evaluation method providing a framework for assessing non-academic impacts. Covers the method’s building blocks and how to assess the efficiency of knowledge exchange.
details.outcomes: A structured plan for assessing and communicating the non-academic impact of your research.

author: Erasmus University Rotterdam

title: Engaged Research Planning for Impact
summary: A clear and concise framework for understanding research impact and how you can start planning for it. Informed by recent literature and international consultation.

details.who: Researchers at the early stages of planning a project or drafting a funding application.
details.what: A guide informed by academic literature and consultation with researchers, policymakers, and funding agency personnel. Provides inspiration and guidance for planning engaged research and drafting funding applications.
details.outcomes: A clearer understanding of research impact and a starting framework for your impact plan.

author: Campus Engage and Irish Universities Association

title: Knowledge Mobilization Modules
summary: Free, online modules on knowledge mobilization topics including an intro to KMb, storytelling for impact, and infographic design. Stand-alone and completable in any order.

details.who: Researchers looking to build practical knowledge mobilization skills during or after their research.
details.what: Freely accessible e-modules, each focused on a specific KMb skill. Step-by-step guidance with tools and additional resources for increased uptake. Apply the training directly to your own work.
details.outcomes: Practical skills in knowledge mobilization, storytelling for impact, and visual communication of research.

author: Research Impact Canada

title: Methods for Inclusive Research
summary: Planning an inclusive research project but not sure how you want to engage your stakeholders? The Action Catalogue is an online decision support tool intented to help you find the method that is best suited for your specific project needs.

details.who: Researchers planning an inclusive research project and want support planning how to engage your stakeholders
details.what: An online decision support tool intended to enable conducting inclusive research, to find the method that is best suited for your specific project needs. The catalogue consists of 57 methods with the common denominator that your focus is research driven by involvement and inclusion.
details.outcomes: A plan for how you will facilitate your stakeholder engagement.

author: Engage 2020

title: Impact Activities Catalogue
summary: Trying to picture what type of research impact you want to make? Anchored by three levels of community engagement, this catalogue helps you brainstorm the type of impact you want to work towards.

details.who: Researchers, project leads, or staff involved in developing, implementing, or evaluating impact initiatives.
details.what: A catalogue describing key societal impact activities across different engagement levels — from academic scholarship and commercialization to academic advising and science activism.
details.outcomes: A clearer picture of what types of impact activities align with your research goals and engagement level.

author: Erasmus University Rotterdam

title: Stakeholder Analysis Matrix Template
summary: Map the people who make research matter. Identify key partners, understand their influence and priorities, and plan how best to engage them throughout your project.

details.who: Researchers and project teams at the planning stage who need to identify and engage stakeholders.
details.what: A practical template to systematically identify stakeholders, assess their influence and interest, and plan effective engagement strategies. Supports stronger partnership-building and strategic impact planning.
details.outcomes: A completed stakeholder map with engagement strategies aligned to the needs of communities, policymakers, and partners.

author: Tools4Dev

title: What is Community-Based Participatory Action Research?
summary: The Action Research Podcast aims to offer unique and valuable insights for the field through accessible and engaging conversations about the “what” “why” and “how” of Action Research.

details.who: Researchers who are planning a community-based research project. This resource was one of many identified as part of a community-based research resource gathering exercise led by Concordia's Office of Community Engagement. See the full list of resources assembled in their zotero here.
details.what: This podcast episode provides researchers with the key definitions and principles of Community-Based Participatory Action Research (CBPAR), and offers advice on how to consider positionality when using this framework. A reference list, including sources on CBPAR, North American case studies, theoretical explanations and suggestions for community work is provided in the description.
details.outcomes: A better understanding of what makes for quality action research or participatory action research.

author: The Action Research Podcast

title: Power Research and Research Tools for Organizers
summary: Through diagrams, reports, and live and recorded training sessions, this resource provides researchers with multiple ways to consider and design power research in the context of community based research, including tools that can be used to visualize power links.

details.who: Researchers who are planning a community-based research project. This resource was one of many identified as part of a community-based research resource gathering exercise led by Concordia's Office of Community Engagement. See the full list of resources assembled in their zotero here.
details.what: Research Tools for Organizers is a training curriculum designed to help you level up your toolkit and bring a new perspective to your campaigns by incorporating practical research techniques and a corporate power analysis into your campaign development.
details.outcomes: A better understanding of power research and ways to support community led campaigns.

author: The Public Accountability Initiative (also know as "Little Sis")
